name: IL-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Mary Miller running with a large financial edge
Challenger Jennifer Todd raised only ~$113k with no outside support
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~96%
model.rationale: The R+20 district, Miller's incumbency and roughly 12-to-1 fundraising advantage leave the Democrat with no evident path, and markets agree at about a 96% Republican win probability. With no polls or expert ratings available, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly -18 stands.
model.watch: A national Democratic wave environment or unexpected Miller controversy could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mary Miller, the incumbent Republican, is favored to hold this heavily Republican southern Illinois district, which leans about 20 points toward the GOP. She has raised over $1.3 million and holds more than $800,000 on hand, while Democratic challenger Jennifer Todd has raised about $113,000 with modest cash reserves and no reported outside spending on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap and incumbency. Prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 96 percent, consistent with a safe Republican rating.
